formulations.label: Oral suspension
formulations.note: Contains sorbitol (2.275 g per 5 mL) and hydroxybenzoates.

src.q: Each 1ml of oral suspension contains 1mg domperidone.
Each 5 ml contains 2.275 g of sorbitol

formulations.label: Tablets
formulations.note: No UK SmPC for a standard 10 mg domperidone tablet was found on emc (the MHRA products database could not be searched: service unavailable). The UK SmPC for domperidone 10 mg orodispersible tablets is used for this form; dose, contraindications and warnings match the suspension SmPC. The orodispersible tablet contains aspartame.

src.q: Each orodispersible tablet contains 10 mg Domperidone (as maleate)
Excipients: 7.5 mg of aspartame (E951)

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Relief of the symptoms of nausea and vomiting, in adults and adolescents 12 years and over weighing 35 kg or more (MHRA: no other indication since 2014).

src.q: Domperidone is indicated for the relief of the symptoms of nausea and vomiting.
domperidone is now authorised for the relief of symptoms of nausea and vomiting only in adults and adolescents 12 years of age or older and weighing 35 kg or more

items.t: MHRA: indication restricted to nausea and vomiting because of cardiac risk; use the lowest effective dose for the shortest possible time; maximum 30 mg in 24 hours; maximum duration usually 1 week.

src.q: Domperidone is now restricted to use in the relief of nausea and vomiting It should be used at the lowest effective dose for the shortest possible time
domperidone should be used at the lowest effective dose for the shortest possible duration and maximum treatment duration should not usually exceed 1 week

items.t: Prescription-only: must not be sold without prescription; a medical assessment is needed first because of cardiac risk.

src.q: Domperidone must not be sold without prescription
people need to have a medical assessment before taking domperidone to determine if it is suitable for them

items.t: Use beyond licensed dose or duration (e.g. Parkinson's disease treatment side effects): take the cardiac risk and interactions into account. Long-term users should be reassessed.

src.q: should be taken into account if there is a clinical need to use it at doses or durations greater than those authorised
Patients currently receiving long-term treatment with domperidone should be reassessed at a routine appointment to advise on treatment continuation, dose change, or cessation

items.t: 10 mg (tablet, or 10 mL of 1 mg/mL suspension) up to three times daily, before meals. Maximum 30 mg (30 mL) per day. Usually no longer than 1 week. Do not double a missed dose.
items.tag: Nausea and vomiting (adults and adolescents ≥ 12 years and ≥ 35 kg)

src.q: 10 ml (of oral suspension containing domperidone 1mg per ml) up to three times per day with a maximum daily dose of 30 ml per day.
One 10mg tablet up to three times per day with a maximum dose of 30 mg per day.
Usually, the maximum treatment duration should not exceed one week.
The dose should not be doubled to make up for a missed dose.

items.t: Liquid: give only with a graduated measuring device (e.g. oral syringe or measuring cup) for dose accuracy.

src.q: Oral liquid formulations of domperidone should only be given via appropriately designed, graduated measuring devices

items.t: Not licensed in children under 12 years or under 35 kg (efficacy not established; a trial in gastroenteritis showed no benefit over placebo). MHRA: consider alternative treatments in children under 12.

src.q: Domperidone is no longer licensed for use in children younger than 12 years or those weighing less than 35 kg.
consider alternative treatments to domperidone in children younger than 12 years of age who need relief of symptoms of nausea and vomiting
The efficacy of domperidone in adolescents 12 years of age and older and weighing less than 35 kg has not been established.

items.t: If a specialist judges off-label use justified in a child under 12, fully inform the patient or carer of benefits and risks.

src.q: the patient or parent/caregiver should be fully informed of the potential benefits and risks of the different options

items.t: Hypersensitivity to domperidone or any excipient.

src.q: Known hypersensitivity to domperidone or any of the excipients

items.t: Prolactin-releasing pituitary tumour (prolactinoma).

src.q: Prolactin-releasing pituitary tumour (prolactinoma).

items.t: Confirmed or suspected phaeochromocytoma (risk of severe hypertension) - new contraindication, MHRA July 2026: stop immediately and switch.

src.q: Confirmed or suspected pheochromocytoma due to the risk of severe hypertension episodes.
patients with confirmed or suspected phaeochromocytoma should stop taking domperidone immediately and be switched to an alternative treatment

items.t: When stimulating gastric motility could be harmful: GI haemorrhage, mechanical obstruction or perforation.

src.q: when stimulation of the gastric motility could be harmful, e.g .,in patients with gastro-intestinal haemorrhage, mechanical obstruction or perforation.

items.t: Moderate (Child-Pugh 7-9) or severe (Child-Pugh > 9) hepatic impairment.

src.q: Domperidone is contraindicated in moderate (Child-Pugh 7 to 9) or severe (Child-Pugh > 9) hepatic impairment

items.t: Known prolonged cardiac conduction intervals (particularly QTc), significant electrolyte disturbance (hypokalaemia, hyperkalaemia, hypomagnesaemia), bradycardia, or underlying cardiac disease such as congestive heart failure.

src.q: Domperidone is contraindicated in patients with known existing prolongation of cardiac conduction intervals, particularly QTc, in patients with significant electrolyte disturbances (hypokalaemia, hyperkalaemia, hypomagnesaemia), or bradycardia

items.t: With QT-prolonging drugs (except apomorphine under strict conditions) and with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors, regardless of their QT effect.

src.q: co-administration with QT-prolonging drugs, at the exception of apomorphine
co-administration with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (regardless of their QT prolonging effects)

items.t: QT prolongation, torsades de pointes, serious ventricular arrhythmia and sudden cardiac death reported. Higher risk: age over 60, daily dose above 30 mg, and QT-prolonging drugs or CYP3A4 inhibitors. Use the lowest effective dose.

src.q: Epidemiological studies showed that domperidone was associated with an increased risk of serious ventricular arrhythmias or sudden cardiac death
A higher risk was observed in patients older than 60 years, patients taking daily doses greater than 30 mg, and patients concurrently taking QT-prolonging drugs or CYP3A4 inhibitors.

items.t: Stop if signs or symptoms of cardiac arrhythmia occur; patients should promptly report cardiac symptoms.

src.q: Treatment with domperidone should be stopped if signs or symptoms occur that may be associated with cardiac arrhythmia, and the patients should consult their physician.

items.t: May unmask phaeochromocytoma: if a patient has an episode of severe hypertension, consider investigating for it.

src.q: be aware that administration of domperidone can unmask phaeochromocytomas. If a patient taking domperidone has an episode of severe hypertension, consider further investigations for phaeochromocytoma

items.t: Severe renal impairment: reduce dosing frequency to once or twice daily (dose may need reducing) and review regularly.

src.q: the dosing frequency of domperidone should be reduced to once or twice daily depending on the severity of the impairment, and the dose may need to be reduced

items.t: Levodopa: plasma levodopa may rise by 30-40% (no levodopa dose change deemed necessary).

src.q: Although no dosage adjustment of levodopa is deemed necessary, an increase of plasma levodopa concentration (max 30-40%) has been observed

items.t: Suspension: contains sorbitol - patients with hereditary fructose intolerance should not take it; hydroxybenzoates may cause (possibly delayed) allergic reactions.

src.q: Patients with hereditary problems of fructose intolerance (HFI) should not take this medicine .
which may cause allergic reactions (possibly delayed)

items.t: Contraindicated with QT-prolonging medicines, e.g. class IA/III antiarrhythmics (amiodarone, sotalol), some antipsychotics (haloperidol), citalopram, escitalopram, erythromycin, levofloxacin, moxifloxacin, methadone (list not exhaustive).

src.q: certain anti-depressants (e.g., citalopram, escitalopram) certain antibiotics (e.g. , erythromycin, levofloxacin, moxifloxacin, spiramycin)
The above list of substances is representative and not exhaustive.

items.t: Contraindicated with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors: protease inhibitors, systemic azole antifungals, some macrolides (erythromycin, clarithromycin). Ketoconazole or erythromycin tripled domperidone levels and prolonged QTc by about 10 ms.

src.q: Potent CYP3A4 inhibitors ( regardless of their QT prolonging effects ), i.e.: protease inhibitors systemic azole antifungals some macrolides (erythromycin, clarithromycin, telithromycin)
Both the Cmax and AUC of domperidone at steady state were increased approximately three-fold in each of these interaction studies.

items.t: Not recommended with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors: diltiazem, verapamil and some macrolides.

src.q: Concomitant use of the following substances is not recommended Moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors i.e. diltiazem, verapamil and some macrolides.

items.t: Caution with drugs causing bradycardia or hypokalaemia, and with azithromycin and roxithromycin.

src.q: Caution with bradycardia and hypokalaemia-inducing drugs, as well as with the following macrolides involved in QT-interval prolongation: azithromycin and roxithromycin

items.t: Suspension SmPC: do not take antacids or antisecretory drugs at the same time - take domperidone before meals and the antacid/antisecretory after meals (lower domperidone bioavailability).

src.q: Antacids or antisecretory agents should not be taken simultaneously with oral formulations of domperidone as they lower the oral bioavailability of domperidone.
Domperidone should be taken before meals and antacids or antisecretory agents after meals.

items.t: Apomorphine: contraindicated unless benefit outweighs risk and the apomorphine SmPC precautions (QT checks, ECG) are strictly followed.

src.q: apomorphine, unless the benefit of the co-administration outweighs the risks, and only if the recommended precautions for co-administration are strictly fulfilled.

items.t: Severe renal impairment (serum creatinine > 6 mg/100 mL, i.e. 0.6 mmol/L): half-life prolonged - give once or twice daily, dose may need reducing; review regularly. No eGFR/CrCl threshold is given.

src.q: Since the elimination half-life of domperidone is prolonged in severe renal impairment (serum creatinine > 6mg/100mL, i.e. 0.6 mmol/L)
Such patients with severe renal impairment should be reviewed regularly

items.t: Contraindicated in moderate (Child-Pugh 7-9) or severe (Child-Pugh > 9) hepatic impairment. Mild (Child-Pugh 5-6): no dose change.

src.q: Domperidone is contraindicated in moderate (Child-Pugh 7 to 9) or severe (Child-Pugh > 9) hepatic impairment
Dose modification in mild (Child-Pugh 5 to 6) hepatic impairment is however not needed

items.t: SmPC: limited human data; animal reproductive toxicity at maternally toxic doses. Use only when justified by the expected benefit.

src.q: There are limited post-marketing data on the use of domperidone in pregnant women.
Domperidone should only be used during pregnancy when justified by the anticipated therapeutic benefit.

items.t: BUMPS: domperidone is one of the options if an antihistamine does not help pregnancy sickness; overall these medicines are considered safe for the baby.

src.q: These include ondansetron (Zofran®), metoclopramide (Maxolon®), and domperidone.
Overall, these medicines are considered safe for your baby.

items.t: SmPC: infants receive < 0.1% of the maternal weight-adjusted dose; adverse (especially cardiac) effects cannot be excluded. Decide whether to stop breastfeeding or domperidone; caution if the infant has QTc risk factors.

src.q: Domperidone is excreted in human milk and breast-fed infants receive less than 0.1 % of the maternal weight-adjusted dose.
Caution should be exercised in case of QTc prolongation risk factors in breast-fed infants.

items.t: SPS: negligible amounts pass into milk; no serious infant effects reported - monitor for GI disturbance or dry mouth. Avoid in the mother if the infant has cardiac disease, severe liver disease or takes interacting medicines.

src.q: Very limited information shows domperidone passes into breast milk in negligible amounts (less than 0.5% of the maternal weight-adjusted dose)
As a precaution, monitor for gastro-intestinal disturbances, or signs of dry mouth , such as difficulty feeding.
If the infant has cardiac disease, severe liver disease or is receiving medicines which may be a problem, then domperidone use in the mother is best avoided.

items.t: SPS (off-licence, low milk supply): only after full assessment; 10 mg three times daily for 7 days then review; do not use higher doses.

src.q: Use 10mg three times daily, initially for 7 days then review.
Doses higher than this should not be used .

reproductive.note: No fertility or contraception statement in the UK SmPCs (1 mg/mL oral suspension, 10 mg orodispersible tablets) or the MHRA Drug Safety Updates checked.

items.t: Common: dry mouth. Uncommon: somnolence, headache, extrapyramidal disorder, diarrhoea, anxiety, agitation, loss of libido, rash, pruritus, urticaria, galactorrhoea, breast pain/tenderness, asthenia.

src.q: Dry mouth Diarrhoea
Somnolence Headache Extrapyramidal disorder
Galactorrhoea Breast pain Breast tenderness

items.t: Ventricular arrhythmias, QTc prolongation, torsade de pointes, sudden cardiac death (frequency not known): stop and seek medical help for palpitations, fainting, chest pain or irregular heartbeat.

src.q: Ventricular arrhythmias Sudden cardiac death QTc prolongation Torsade de Pointes
Seek medical attention immediately if you experience heart-related symptoms such as irregular heartbeat or fainting while taking domperidone

items.t: Anaphylactic reaction including shock; angioedema (frequency not known).

src.q: Anaphylactic reaction (including anaphylactic shock)

items.t: Severe hypertension in phaeochromocytoma.

src.q: a small number of reports have been received relating to severe episodes of hypertension in patients with phaeochromocytoma

items.t: Convulsion, oculogyric crisis, urinary retention (frequency not known).

src.q: Convulsion Restless legs syndrome*

items.t: Before prescribing, check for cardiac disease, QT prolongation, bradycardia, electrolyte disturbance, moderate/severe liver disease and interacting medicines (QT-prolonging drugs, CYP3A4 inhibitors).

src.q: Do not prescribe domperidone in people with bradycardia, congenital QT prolongation, underlying cardiac diseases or receiving other medications known to prolong QT interval or potent CYP3A4 inhibitors.

items.t: SPS: with non-modifiable patient and medicine risk factors, monitor ECG, magnesium and potassium before and during treatment.

src.q: Monitor ECG, magnesium and potassium before and during treatment in people with non-modifiable patient and medicine risk factors.

items.t: Review at 1 week (maximum usual duration); reassess any long-term use.

src.q: maximum treatment duration should not usually exceed 1 week
Patients currently receiving long-term treatment with domperidone should be reassessed at a routine appointment

items.t: Stop if arrhythmia symptoms occur, or immediately if phaeochromocytoma is confirmed or suspected.

src.q: Treatment with domperidone should be stopped if signs or symptoms occur that may be associated with cardiac arrhythmia
patients with confirmed or suspected phaeochromocytoma should stop taking domperidone immediately

items.t: Take 15-30 minutes before meals (absorption delayed if taken after meals).

src.q: It is recommended to take oral domperidone 15-30 minutes before meals. If taken after meals, absorption of the drug is somewhat delayed.

items.t: Take before meals (absorption is delayed if taken after meals). The UK SmPC used is for an orodispersible tablet; its place-on-the-tongue method does not apply to a standard tablet.

src.q: It is recommended to take Epzit 10 mg Orodispersible Tablets before meals.
If taken after meals, absorption of the drug is somewhat delayed.

items.t: Use only for short periods for nausea and vomiting. Get medical help at once for irregular heartbeat, fainting, dizziness, chest pain or palpitations.

src.q: Domperidone should only be used for short periods of time to treat nausea and vomiting
Talk to a doctor straight away if you experience dizziness; fainting; chest pain; or a rapid, fluttering, or pounding heartbeat while taking domperidone.

items.t: Seek urgent help for signs of very high blood pressure (persistent headache, blurred vision, breathlessness, chest pain).

src.q: Symptoms can include, but are not limited to: persistent headache, blurred vision, shortness of breath and chest pain.

items.t: May cause drowsiness - do not drive or use machines until you know how it affects you.

src.q: patients should be advised not to drive or use machinery or engage in other activities requiring mental alertness and coordination until they have established how domperidone affects them
